TASK ID: exact-cover-to-subset-sum

USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from Exact Cover to Subset Sum. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Exact Cover and TARGET is Subset Sum. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = ExactCover
Exact Cover.

Instance: {"universe_size": u, "sets": [[element, ...], ...]}
  * The universe is the elements 0..u-1.
  * Each set lists distinct elements of the universe, in any order. A set
    may be empty, and the same set may appear more than once.

Yes iff some of the sets contain every element of the universe exactly
once: the chosen sets are pairwise disjoint and their union is the whole
universe.

Edge cases: u = 0 is yes (choose no sets). Empty sets never matter. Two
copies of the same non-empty set can never both be chosen.

TARGET = SubsetSum
Subset Sum.

Instance: {"numbers": [a1, a2, ...], "target": t}
  * The numbers are non-negative integers of any size; values may repeat.
  * The target is any integer.

Yes iff some sub-list of the numbers (each position used at most once)
sums to exactly t.

Edge cases: t = 0 is always yes (the empty sub-list). t < 0 is always
no. An empty list is yes only for t = 0.

INPUT FILES: ["problems.py"]
WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-khejznt6

The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

You may read files such as problems.py, but do not run, execute or test any code. Write reduce.py, then submit.
Do not merely describe code: leave the files at those exact paths.

{"command":"cd /tmp/reduction-khejznt6 && cat <<'EOF' > reduce.py
"""Polynomial-time reduction from Exact Cover to Subset Sum.

Idea
----
Let ``u`` be the universe size and ``m`` the number of available sets.  Work in
base ``B = m + 1``.  Encode an element ``e`` by the digit position ``e``.

* For every set ``S`` emit the number ``n(S) = sum_{e in S} B**e``.
* The target is the number whose every digit (positions ``0..u-1``) is ``1``:
  ``t = sum_{e=0}^{u-1} B**e``.

Choosing a sub-list of the emitted numbers corresponds to choosing a
sub-collection of sets.  The digit at position ``e`` of the sum is exactly the
number of chosen sets that contain element ``e``.  Because at most ``m`` sets
are chosen, every digit lies in ``0..m < B``, so there is never a carry between
digit positions.  Hence the sum equals ``t`` iff every element is contained in
exactly one chosen set, i.e. iff the chosen sets form an exact cover.

Edge cases
----------
* ``u = 0``: the target is ``0`` (empty sum), which Subset Sum always accepts.
* Empty sets become the number ``0`` and can be added or omitted freely; they
  never change the sum, matching the fact that they never matter.
* Duplicate sets become equal numbers; taking two copies would put a ``2`` in
  some digit, so they cannot both be used (as required).
* ``m = 0`` (no sets): the base is ``1``, the target is ``u`` and the number
  list is empty, so the answer is yes iff ``u = 0``.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    """Return a Subset Sum instance equivalent to the Exact Cover instance."""
    universe_size = instance["universe_size"]
    sets = instance["sets"]

    m = len(sets)
    base = m + 1

    numbers = []
    for s in sets:
        value = 0
        for e in s:
            value += base ** e
        numbers.append(value)

    target = 0
    power = 1
    for _ in range(universe_size):
        target += power
        power *= base

    return {"numbers": numbers, "target": target}
EOF
